about.title: A body, revealed.
about.lede: Explore the adult male reference anatomy from BodyParts3D.
about.sectionBody: 2,234 individual meshes and 3,432 named concepts from an adult male reference anatomy.
about.scope: This reference does not contain every human structure or variation. Named concepts can contain multiple pieces; each source mesh is rendered once.
about.detail: Colors and system groupings are designed for exploration. The geometry is simplified for the web, and short explanations provide general educational context. This is an anatomical reference, not a diagnostic or surgical tool.

skeletal.name: Skeleton
skeletal.description: Bones form the supporting framework of the body, protect organs, and provide attachment points for muscles. Their internal tissue also stores minerals and produces blood cells.

muscular.name: Muscles
muscular.description: Skeletal muscles generate movement by pulling on their attachments. Together with tendons, they move joints, stabilize posture, and produce heat.

cardiac.name: Heart
cardiac.description: The heart is a muscular pump with four chambers. Its valves direct blood forward through the pulmonary and systemic circuits.

sensory.name: Sensory organs
sensory.description: These structures contribute to special senses, including sight, hearing, and balance. Their specialized tissues detect stimuli and work with the nervous system to convey information.

arterial.name: Arteries
arterial.description: The heart drives blood through the circulation. Arteries carry blood away from the heart to supply tissues or, in the pulmonary circuit, to the lungs.

venous.name: Veins
venous.description: Veins return blood toward the heart. Superficial and deep networks collect blood from the tissues; the pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood back from the lungs.

nervous.name: Nervous system
nervous.description: The brain, spinal cord, and peripheral nerves carry and process signals. They support sensation, movement, coordination, and automatic regulation of body functions.

respiratory.name: Respiratory
respiratory.description: The airways conduct air to the lungs, where oxygen and carbon dioxide move between air and blood. Breathing depends on pressure changes produced by respiratory muscles.

digestive.name: Digestive
digestive.description: The digestive tract breaks down food, absorbs nutrients and water, and moves waste onward. Accessory organs contribute bile and digestive enzymes.

urinary.name: Urinary
urinary.description: The kidneys filter blood and regulate fluid, electrolyte, and acid–base balance. Urine travels through the ureters to the bladder and exits through the urethra.

lymphatic.name: Lymphatic
lymphatic.description: Lymphatic vessels return excess tissue fluid to the circulation. Lymph nodes and other lymphoid organs support immune surveillance and responses.

endocrine.name: Endocrine
endocrine.description: Endocrine organs release hormones into the blood to coordinate processes such as metabolism, growth, stress responses, and reproduction.

reproductive.name: Reproductive
reproductive.description: The male reproductive structures represented here contribute to sperm production, maturation, transport, and the production of sex hormones.

integumentary.name: Body surface
integumentary.description: The body surface provides an outer anatomical reference. The integumentary system forms a protective barrier and contributes to sensation and temperature regulation.

connective.name: Connective tissue
connective.description: Cartilage, ligaments, and other connective tissues support, connect, and separate structures. Their roles include stabilizing joints and distributing mechanical loads.

explanations.heart: A muscular pump in the chest. Its right side sends blood to the lungs; its left side sends blood through the systemic circulation.
explanations.liver: A large organ beneath the right side of the diaphragm. It processes absorbed nutrients, produces bile, and synthesizes many proteins carried in the blood.
explanations.brain: The central organ of the nervous system. Its interconnected regions support perception, movement, memory, language, and the regulation of bodily functions.
explanations.stomach: A muscular chamber between the esophagus and small intestine. It stores and mixes food with acid and enzymes before releasing it into the duodenum.
explanations.spleen: A lymphoid organ in the upper left abdomen. It filters blood, removes aging blood cells, and participates in immune responses.
explanations.pancreas: An abdominal organ with digestive and endocrine roles. It supplies enzymes to the small intestine and releases hormones including insulin and glucagon.
explanations.urinary bladder: A muscular reservoir in the pelvis that stores urine arriving from the kidneys through the ureters.
explanations.trachea: The main airway connecting the larynx to the bronchi. Its cartilage supports keep the airway open during breathing.
explanations.diaphragm: A broad muscle separating the chest and abdomen. When it contracts, it increases chest volume and helps draw air into the lungs.
explanations.skull: The bony structure atop the spine that encases and protects the brain while forming the facial framework.
explanations.sternum: A flat, elongated bone in the center of the chest, connecting the clavicles and costal cartilages.
explanations.clavicle: An S-shaped long bone connecting the upper limb to the trunk, acting as a horizontal strut for the shoulder.
explanations.scapula: A triangular flat bone on the upper posterior thorax that forms the shoulder girdle.
explanations.humerus: The long bone of the upper arm; its head forms the shoulder joint, its distal end forms the elbow.
explanations.radius: The lateral (thumb-side) long bone of the forearm; its distal end forms the wrist joint.
explanations.ulna: The medial (pinky-side) long bone of the forearm; its proximal end forms the hinge of the elbow.
explanations.femur: The longest and strongest bone in the body, running from the hip to the knee and bearing body weight.
explanations.patella: A sesamoid bone in the quadriceps tendon at the front of the knee, increasing leverage.
explanations.tibia: The main weight-bearing long bone of the lower leg; forms the knee above and ankle below.
explanations.fibula: The slender lateral bone of the lower leg, mainly a muscle attachment that does not bear weight.
explanations.vertebral column: The axial skeleton of 24 vertebrae plus the sacrum and coccyx that protects the spinal cord.
explanations.rib 1: The shortest and most curved rib, articulating posteriorly with T1 and anteriorly with the manubrium.
explanations.rib: One of 24 slender curved bones forming the thoracic cage; protect thoracic organs and enable breathing.
explanations.manubrium of sternum: The broad upper part of the sternum that articulates with the clavicles and first two ribs.
explanations.body of sternum: The longest central portion of the sternum, articulating with costal cartilages 2 through 7.
explanations.xiphoid process: The small cartilaginous lower tip of the sternum, fusing with the body in adulthood.
explanations.ilium: The broad upper wing of the hip bone forming the lateral pelvic wall.
explanations.ischium: The posteroinferior portion of the hip bone that bears weight when sitting.
explanations.pubis: The anteroinferior part of the hip bone; the two pubic bones meet at the pubic symphysis.
explanations.biceps brachii: A two-headed muscle on the front of the upper arm; flexes the elbow and supinates the forearm.
explanations.triceps brachii: A three-headed muscle on the back of the upper arm; the only extensor of the elbow.
explanations.deltoid: A triangular muscle capping the shoulder; the prime mover for arm abduction.
explanations.pectoralis major: A large fan-shaped muscle of the upper chest; adducts, flexes, and medially rotates the humerus.
explanations.latissimus dorsi: A broad muscle of the lower back; extends, adducts, and medially rotates the humerus.
explanations.trapezius: A diamond-shaped muscle of the upper back and neck; controls the scapula and supports the arm.
explanations.sternocleidomastoid: A strap muscle of the anterolateral neck; one-sided contraction tilts and rotates the head.
explanations.rectus abdominis: A paired vertical muscle on the front of the abdomen; the prime trunk flexor.
explanations.external oblique muscle: The outermost flat abdominal muscle; rotates and laterally flexes the trunk.
explanations.internal oblique muscle: A flat abdominal muscle deep to the external oblique; rotates the trunk with the opposite side.
explanations.transversus abdominis: The deepest abdominal muscle with horizontal fibers; increases intra-abdominal pressure.
explanations.quadriceps femoris: A four-part muscle group on the front of the thigh; the strongest knee extensors.
explanations.biceps femoris: A posterior thigh muscle; flexes the knee and extends the hip.
explanations.semitendinosus: A posteromedial thigh muscle; extends the hip and flexes the knee.
explanations.semimembranosus: A deep posteromedial thigh muscle that extends the hip and flexes the knee.
explanations.gastrocnemius: The two-headed calf muscle; plantar-flexes the ankle and assists knee flexion.
explanations.soleus: A deep calf muscle that, with the gastrocnemius, plantar-flexes the ankle.
explanations.tibialis anterior: An anterior leg muscle; dorsiflexes the ankle and inverts the foot.
explanations.gluteus maximus: The largest and most superficial buttock muscle; the most powerful hip extensor.
explanations.gluteus medius: A fan-shaped mid-buttock muscle; abducts the hip.
explanations.masseter: A deep cheek muscle; the prime mover for jaw closure.
explanations.temporalis: A fan-shaped muscle of the temporal fossa; elevates and retracts the mandible.
explanations.orbicularis oculi: A ring-shaped muscle around the eye orbit; closes the eyelids.
explanations.orbicularis oris: A ring-shaped muscle around the mouth; closes the lips.
explanations.sartorius: The body's longest muscle; crosses the thigh obliquely from hip to medial knee.
explanations.lung: A paired conical respiratory organ in the thorax; the main site of gas exchange.
explanations.right lung: Has three lobes and connects to the trachea via the right main bronchus.
explanations.left lung: Has two lobes and is smaller than the right due to the cardiac notch.
explanations.kidney: A paired retroperitoneal organ that produces urine and regulates fluid and electrolyte balance.
explanations.adrenal gland: An endocrine gland capping each kidney; secretes catecholamines and corticosteroids.
explanations.thyroid gland: An H-shaped endocrine gland in the front of the neck; regulates metabolism.
explanations.esophagus: A muscular tube behind the trachea that conveys food from pharynx to stomach.
explanations.small intestine: A long coiled digestive tube divided into duodenum, jejunum, and ileum; the main site of nutrient absorption.
explanations.large intestine: The wider terminal digestive tube; absorbs water and forms feces.
explanations.duodenum: The C-shaped first segment of the small intestine that receives bile and pancreatic juice.
explanations.jejunum: The middle segment of the small intestine; the main site of nutrient absorption.
explanations.ileum: The terminal segment of the small intestine; joins the large intestine at the ileocecal valve.
explanations.cecum: The first part of the large intestine in the right iliac fossa, into which the ileum opens.
explanations.vermiform appendix: A worm-shaped lymphoid projection from the posteromedial cecum.
explanations.gallbladder: A pear-shaped sac beneath the liver that stores and concentrates bile.
explanations.tongue: A muscular organ in the floor of the mouth; involved in chewing, swallowing, speech, and taste.
explanations.nose: The facial prominence that begins the respiratory tract and houses the olfactory organ.
explanations.ear: The organ of hearing and balance, divided into external, middle, and internal ear.
explanations.eye: The visual organ within the orbit that transduces light into neural signals.
explanations.skin: The body's largest organ; provides protection, sensation, and thermoregulation.
explanations.aorta: The largest artery, ascending from the left ventricle and supplying the entire systemic circulation.
explanations.common carotid artery: The main neck artery that bifurcates into internal and external carotid arteries.
explanations.internal carotid artery: A branch of the common carotid that enters the skull to supply the anterior brain and eye.
explanations.external carotid artery: A branch of the common carotid that supplies the face, scalp, and neck.
explanations.subclavian artery: The artery beneath the clavicle; supplies the upper limb and part of the brain.
explanations.vertebral artery: An artery ascending through the cervical transverse foramina to enter the skull and form the basilar artery.
explanations.axillary artery: The continuation of the subclavian artery through the axilla, supplying the shoulder and chest wall.
explanations.brachial artery: The main artery of the upper arm; the common site for blood-pressure measurement.
explanations.femoral artery: The main artery of the thigh; the continuation of the external iliac below the inguinal ligament.
explanations.popliteal artery: The continuation of the femoral artery through the popliteal fossa, dividing into tibial arteries.
explanations.common iliac artery: A terminal branch of the abdominal aorta at L4; divides into internal and external iliac arteries.
explanations.superior vena cava: Formed by the union of the brachiocephalic veins; drains upper-body blood into the right atrium.
explanations.inferior vena cava: The largest vein; formed by the union of the common iliac veins and drains into the right atrium.
explanations.internal jugular vein: The deep neck vein that, with the subclavian, forms the brachiocephalic vein.
explanations.external jugular vein: A superficial neck vein draining the scalp and face.
explanations.great saphenous vein: The body's longest superficial vein; runs along the medial leg and is commonly used as a graft source.
explanations.portal vein: Formed by the union of the splenic and superior mesenteric veins; carries nutrient-rich blood to the liver.
explanations.thyrocervical trunk: The first branch of the subclavian artery; gives off the inferior thyroid and other neck arteries.
explanations.costal cartilage: The hyaline cartilage linking ribs to the sternum; allows rib cage flexibility in breathing.
explanations.intervertebral disc: The fibrocartilaginous cushion between adjacent vertebral bodies; absorbs shock and permits motion.
explanations.shoulder: The region connecting the upper limb to the trunk; centered on the glenohumeral joint and its surrounding muscles.
explanations.elbow: The hinge joint between the upper arm and forearm, formed by the humerus, radius, and ulna.
explanations.wrist: The complex joint between the forearm and the hand, formed by the radius and carpal bones.
explanations.hip: The ball-and-socket joint between the femur and the acetabulum of the pelvis.
explanations.knee: The body's largest joint, formed by the femur, tibia, and patella.
explanations.ankle: The joint between the leg and foot, formed by the tibia, fibula, and talus.
